summary: Support addNum and findMedian on a growing stream.
mainInsight: Split the numbers into a lower half (max-heap) and an upper half (min-heap) of balanced sizes; the median is the top of one heap or the average of both tops. Each insertion rebalances in O(log n).

approaches.name: Sorted list insertion
approaches.summary: Insert with bisect.insort; read the middle.

approaches.name: Two heaps
approaches.summary: max-heap for the lower half, min-heap for the upper half, sizes differ by at most 1.

approaches.name: Counting array / buckets
approaches.summary: When values are bounded, count occurrences and walk the counts.

personalSolution.approach: Two heaps (max-heap lower half, min-heap upper half)

promptVariants: Which structure combination gives O(log n) insert and O(1) median?
How do you track the median of a stream?
options: A max-heap of the lower half and a min-heap of the upper half
A single min-heap that stores every number added and pops the top
A hash map of counts keyed by value, scanned in sorted order per query
A stack kept in sorted order, with the median at the middle index
cards.answer: A max-heap of the lower half and a min-heap of the upper half
cards.explanation: The two heap roots are the middle elements of the sorted order.

incorrectOptionExplanations.A hash map of counts keyed by value, sca: Needs a scan to find the middle.

promptVariants: What must always hold between the heaps?
cards.answer: Every element of the lower half (max-heap) is <= every element of the upper half (min-heap), and their sizes differ by at most one (in your code the min-heap holds the extra element). Then the median is the min-heap root or the average of both roots.
cards.explanation: Rebalancing after each insert restores both invariants.

promptVariants: Time of addNum with two heaps: ___
Complete the statement: Time of addNum with two heaps: ___
cards.explanation: A constant number of heap pushes/pops.

promptVariants: How much memory do the heaps use and what is the cost of findMedian?
cards.answer: O(n) total across both heaps; findMedian only reads the roots, O(1).
cards.explanation: All numbers must be stored because any may become the median.

promptVariants: Trace addNum(num): why push to the min-heap, pop it into the max-heap, then rebalance?
What does this three-step dance guarantee?
cards.code:
heappush(self.minHeap, num)
val = heappop(self.minHeap)
heappush(self.maxHeap, -val)
if len(self.maxHeap) > len(self.minHeap):
    val = heappop(self.maxHeap)
    heappush(self.minHeap, -val)
cards.answer: Pushing into the upper half and popping its smallest hands the max-heap the smallest of the upper half including num, so every lower element stays <= every upper element. Then, if the lower half got bigger, its largest is moved back to the upper half, keeping the size relationship (min-heap has the extra element).
keyPoints: Route through the upper half to keep ordering
cards.explanation: Max-heap is simulated by negating values.

promptVariants: When is the median the average of the two heap roots, and when a single root?
How do the heap sizes tell you which formula to use?
options: Even count: average both roots; odd: the larger heap's root
Always average the two roots, whatever the sizes
Always the min-heap root, whatever the sizes
Always the max-heap root, whatever the sizes
cards.answer: Even count: average both roots; odd: the larger heap's root
cards.explanation: Even count means two middle elements; odd count has a single middle in the larger heap.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Always average the two roots, whatever t: Odd counts have one middle value.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Always the max-heap root, whatever the s: In this design the extra element lives in the min-heap.
